newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-JONAH LOMU PLANNING INTERNATIONAL COMEBACK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-JONAH LOMU PLANNING INTERNATIONAL COMEBACK.

text.p: New Zealand rugby union star Jonah Lomu is planning to resume his playing career next month and hopes to make the All Blacks' end-of-season tour to Britain and Ireland.

The giant winger has not played since 1996 when he was diagnosed with a rare kidney disease, but he told a business luncheon in Sydney on Thursday that he expects to make a comeback as early as next month.

Lomu, 24, said his first target was to compete for Counties Manukau at the New Zealand Provincial Championships from August to October. Then he would press his claims for selection in the squad to tour Britain and Ireland in November and December.
"My main priority first of all is just to get back into playing football," Lomu said.
"I'm targetting the National County Championships later this year then hopefully, if everything goes all right, the All Blacks end-of-season tour.
"That would be a great bonus for me and I would be more than pleased if I was to make it, I'd be jumping for joy."

Lomu burst onto the international scene in 1994 and quickly established himself as the biggest drawcard in the game with a series of devasting performances at the 1995 World Cup in South Africa. At 1.96 metres (six foot five inches) and 118 kg (260 lb), he dwarfed most of his opponents.
His most memorable performance came in the semifinals against England at Newlands Stadium in Cape Town where he scored four tries to secure New Zealand's place in the final.
Lomu struggled to reproduce that form during the 1996 season, however, and was eventually diagnosed as suffering from nephrotic syndrome, a rare kidney disorder.
He was ordered to stop playing or training for at least six months, but remained confident he would eventually make a comeback.
"It came as a great shock at the time," Lomu said on Thursday. "But there was nothing I could do about it except rest like I was told."
The New Zealand Provincial Championships begin on August 15 with Counties Manukau scheduled to play their first game two days later against North Harbour.
The All Blacks travel to Britain and Ireland for a nine-match tour starting on November 8.
The tour includes two tests against England and one each against Ireland and Wales.
